doc.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23

chapter: Kansas City, Chicago and California bands
title: White Horse Tavern in Kansas City, then Chicago and California
summary: He left Moten to make more money at a Kansas City tavern, then played with the Robinson Syncopators in Chicago and moved to Los Angeles, where he played in many bands.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: No, I didn't stay with them that long. Oh, yeah. I found out I could make more money playing in a tavern. A place called the White Horse Tavern on 82nd and Truth. In which town?

In Kansas City. Yeah. I stayed there about a little over a year and I left there and went to Chicago. Yeah. And I played with the Robinson Syncopators in Chicago for about a year around there and I left and came to California. Who else was in this Syncopators? Oh, I don't know all those different guys. They're from Chicago. Oh, yeah. I know. I only played with them for about a month or so, then I gigged around quite a bit, you know. And then I left and came to California. Came to Los Angeles. Yeah. Since that I guess I played in a hundred bands. Yeah. Played with Kay Ory, Mud Carey, Lionel Hampton. Oh Lionel. Yeah. Leon René. Oh, and I guess I made about a hundred pitches playing music for about a hundred pitches and like that and I went on about twenty-five or twenty-eight jazz concerts with Ory, with Kit Ory. We had to leave here, go to San Francisco and I played around here with them for about three years, Joe Dansberg, Gideon Honoré, myself, Eddie Garland.
